groups.title: Syrup (A32900ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as supportive treatment for acute and chronic liver disease, for mild liver failure (loss of liver function) and for cirrhosis of the liver.
groups.usage: Take 1 bottle at a time, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. Press the raised part of the upper cap all the way down, shake well so that the powder and the liquid mix thoroughly, then turn the upper cap to the left to open it and take the contents.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney dysfunction, hepatic coma or a disorder of amino acid metabolism (especially an inherited enzyme deficiency), or if you have or have had a myocardial infarction.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

groups.title: Capsule (188601ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for peripheral nerve disorder.
groups.usage: Adults: take 6 capsules (1,500 μg) in 1 day, divided into 3 doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, if you take H2 receptor blockers over a long period, or if you have drunk a large amount of alcohol for 2 weeks or more. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with most antibiotics including chloramphenicol and aminoglycosides, or with methotrexate, pyrimethamine, colchicine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone or para-aminosalicylic acid.

If loss of appetite, nausea, diarrhoea or rash occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (C20800ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, indigestion, overeating, a feeling of food not going down, nausea and vomiting.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 bottle (75 mL) at a time. Those aged 11 years and over but under 15 years: take 2/3 bottle (50 mL) at a time. Those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years: take 1/2 bottle (37.5 mL) at a time. Those aged 5 years and over but under 8 years: take 1/3 bottle (25 mL) at a time. Those aged 3 years and over but under 5 years: take 1/4 bottle (18.75 mL) at a time. Those aged 1 year and over but under 3 years: take 1/5 bottle (15 mL) at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Babies under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had it, or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (165303ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for disorders of the peripheral arterial circulation (intermittent claudication), dizziness, tinnitus (ringing in the ears) of vascular and degenerative origin, and organic brain dysfunction with dementia-type symptoms such as tinnitus, headache, reduced memory, difficulty concentrating, low mood and dizziness.
groups.usage: Adults: for disorders of the peripheral arterial circulation, dizziness and tinnitus, take 1 tablet (40 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, or 2 tablets (80 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day. For organic brain dysfunction, take 1 to 2 tablets (40 to 80 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day, or 3 tablets (120 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child aged 12 years or under, if you have high blood pressure that needs specific treatment, if you are pregnant, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are breast-feeding, if you have a bleeding disorder, or if you are due to have surgery. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 3 months of use, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anticoagulants (for example phenprocoumon, warfarin) or antiplatelet medicines (for example clopidogrel, acetylsalicylic acid and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines).

If mild gastrointestinal discomfort, headache, an allergic skin reaction, dizziness or itching rarely occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated tablet (E06900ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite (reduced appetite), abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 4 tablets at a time, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (on an empty stomach). At first take the smallest amount, and then increase or decrease it little by little while watching the form and condition of the stool. Do not chew the tablet.
groups.caution:
People with an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), children aged 7 years and under, and people with a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not take this medicine.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure; if your blood pressure is high or you are an older person; or if you have heart or kidney trouble.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Unless it is genuinely needed, it is best that children aged 10 years and under avoid taking it.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after an antacid or after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, cramping, a fall in the amount of urine, swelling of the face, hands or feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache or muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A17200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for brittle hair, for poor growth and poor nutrition of the finger and toe nails, and as an aid to the healing of injuries to the cornea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 4 tablets in 1 day, with a meal.
groups.caution:
People with severe kidney dysfunction, hepatic coma, cystinuria, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not take this medicine. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with levodopa.

If nausea occurs from time to time, or rarely diarrhoea, loss of appetite, thirst, mild abdominal pain or a feeling of abdominal bloating, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (462300ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Children aged 8 to 14 years: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Take it after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
For infants and young children aged 7 years and under, use the syrup form instead.
Drowsiness may occur when it is taken, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other cough and expectorant medicines, cold medicines, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines) or sedatives.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (110701ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, to prevent the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (those with several risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, a high cholesterol level, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time in 1 day. This medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, so it may be taken before a meal with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory medicines or antirheumatic medicines; if you have peptic ulcer, aspirin asthma now or in the past, haemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe heart failure or a tendency to bleed; if you are receiving methotrexate at a dose of 15 mg or more per week; or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy. In the first and second trimesters, do not take this medicine unless it is genuinely needed.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have kidney disorder, impaired cardiovascular or circulatory function (kidney blood-vessel disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like), liver disorder, abnormal heart function or bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or under; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or Reye's syndrome; if the user is a child aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza; or if you have gout.
Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell the doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are to have surgery (including dental surgery).
Be careful not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or salicylate preparations, or with methotrexate at a dose of 15 mg or more per week, as bleeding may increase or kidney function may fall.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, thrombolytic medicines, other antiplatelet medicines, medicines that stop bleeding, medicines for diabetes (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), medicines that promote the excretion of uric acid (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemic corticosteroid preparations (other than hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy in Addison's disease), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations.
Do not mix it with alkaline preparations (for example sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that readily take up moisture.
Taken together with alcohol it increases damage to the lining of the digestive tract, and the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

If shock symptoms (for example difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, hives), an asthma attack, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, heart and breathing problems, and from time to time rash, swelling, hives, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis) or, rarely, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anaemia, anaemia, a fall in white cells, a fall in platelets, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), noises in the ear, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation or liver disorder occurs, or very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney disorder, acute kidney failure, over-breathing, metabolic acidosis, an excessive fall in body temperature, collapse or cold limbs, stop taking it at once and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting may occur.

groups.title: Oral liquid (D64900ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as supportive treatment for megaloblastic anaemia; for pregnancy, the period after delivery, breast-feeding and the recovery period after an illness; for deficiency syndromes caused by a lack of particular nutrients or by an unbalanced diet; for the after-effects of hepatitis and reduced liver function; as supportive treatment in toxic infective states; and during treatment with antibiotics.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 vials in 1 day, before meals. To take it, remove the outer plastic cap and press the inner cap so that the powder held in the double stopper falls into the liquid in the bottle, then shake well for about 20 seconds to mix.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you have cancer.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if you have liver disease or epilepsy, or if you are short of folic acid.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
It can turn the urine yellow and so affect laboratory test results.
Take it immediately after the powder and the liquid have been mixed, or within 24 hours.

Do not take it together with levodopa or hydantoins.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with chloramphenicol, cycloserine, ethionamide, hydralazine, isoniazid, penicillamine, immunosuppressants, oestrogens, anticonvulsants (phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, sodium valproate, carbamazepine, barbiturates and the like), methotrexate, sulfasalazine, lithium, nitrous oxide, ethanol, aspirin, tricyclic antidepressants or phenothiazine medicines, or probenecid.

If erythema, rash, itching, hives, an allergic reaction including wheezing, anxiety, confusion, sleep disturbance, dizziness, headache, loss of appetite, queasiness, abdominal bloating and wind, a feeling of discomfort or irritability occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (208701ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent and treat pantothenic acid deficiency: to supply pantothenic acid where the need for it is increased and intake from food is not enough, such as in wasting disease, an overactive thyroid, pregnancy and breast-feeding; and for high blood fats, sluggish constipation, the prevention and treatment of side effects caused by streptomycin and kanamycin, acute and chronic eczema, and improvement of the platelet count and bleeding tendency in blood disorders, where a lack of pantothenic acid or a disturbance of its metabolism is thought to be involved.
groups.usage: Adults: take 30 to 180 mg as pantethine in 1 day, divided into 1 to 3 doses. For blood disorders and sluggish constipation, take 300 to 600 mg in 1 day, divided into 1 to 3 doses. For high blood fats, take 600 mg in 1 day, divided into 3 doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Food Yellow No. 203.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If diarrhoea, loose stools, nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating or loss of appetite occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E56900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life; for poor growth of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; for the relief of dryness of the eyes and for night blindness; for the relief of stiff shoulders and neck, numbness of the hands and feet and cold hands and feet in disorders of the peripheral circulation and at the menopause; for beriberi, tired eyes, neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); for the relief of angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and over and adults: take 2 tablets at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day can cause birth defects. Women in the first 3 months of pregnancy, or who may be pregnant, must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis (a generalised inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or kidney stones; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age or a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats normally; if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; if you have gout; or if you have or have had kidney stones.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, levodopa or oral contraceptives containing oestrogen.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening, loose stools, stomatitis, dermatitis, an unpleasant smell of sweat or breath, hair loss, impatience, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding becomes heavier or bleeding lasts a long time, or in people who are short of folic acid, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C and of zinc, with relief of dry eyes, night blindness, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, and mouth and skin inflammation

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, a low protein level in the blood or gout; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, low blood pressure, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain or swelling of the lungs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D35900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, shoulder pain, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it up to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should use ibuprofen only after careful consideration and should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day). People with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consider carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or oedema; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are unable to take fluid in; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, diuretics, low-dose aspirin, preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, a fall in the amount of urine with swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis and the like), or very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, a photosensitivity reaction of unknown frequency, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (123844ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum (phlegm) in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, bronchiectasis and pharyngitis, for the drainage of pus in chronic sinusitis, and for the drainage of fluid in secretory otitis media (of the middle ear).
groups.usage: Adults: at the start take 15 mL (750 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day; when symptoms improve, take 10 mL (500 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Those aged 13 years and over but 18 years and under: take 5 mL to 10 mL (250 to 500 mg) at a time, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Those aged 6 years and over but 12 years and under: take 5 mL (250 mg) at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Those aged 2 years and over but 5 years and under: take 5 mL to 10 mL (250 to 500 mg) in 1 day, divided into 4 doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if you are an older person, if you have liver disorder or heart disorder, or if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had it.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with antibiotics or with syrups containing trimetoquinol hydrochloride.

If nausea, vomiting, a feeling of abdominal bloating, gastrointestinal bleeding or heartburn rarely occurs, or from time to time loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or thirst, or stomatitis in sensitive people, rash, erythema (red patches) or eczema, or rarely headache, or rhinitis in sensitive people, or from time to time itching, palpitations, runny nose or a feeling of pressure over the whole body, or Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), liver dysfunction with a rise in AST, ALT, ALP and LDH, jaundice or shock, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.caution:
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, a low protein level in the blood, gout or kidney stones; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you are short of folic acid. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. groups.title: Tablet (C88100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life; for the relief of dryness of the eyes and for night blindness (poor sight at night); for poor growth of the bones and teeth; and for the prevention of rickets.
groups.usage: Children aged 8 years and over and adults: take 2 tablets at a time. Those aged 36 months and over but under 8 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day. After a meal, let it dissolve in the mouth or chew it.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day can cause birth defects. Women in the first 3 months of pregnancy, or who may be pregnant, must not take it. This medicine contains aspartame, which is broken down in the body to phenylalanine, so people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis (a generalised inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats normally; if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; if you have or have had gout or kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or cardiac glycosides. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening, loose stools, low blood pressure, flushing of the face, an irregular heartbeat, red patches, cardiac arrest or reduced function of the central nervous system occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
